caveats: One GNN test look was already used. The GNN team looked once at these splits with these exact prediction files (LOOKS.md, test 1 of 2) and published the AUROCs, so the GNN's held-out performance was known before this analysis; nothing here was tuned. Plan §0 also says LLM protocol (b) on the held-out splits was evaluated earlier (68744e2).

Deviation from the given file list: the committed gnn_opt/preds/eval hgb_bag+graph.csv, hgb_clock.csv and oracle_risk+clock.csv cover night_val only (720 rows, 0 held-out rows). I refit them on night_train with the harness's baselines.py specs. clock and oracle reproduce the committed val predictions bit for bit (so does the edge monitor). bag+graph does not: val AUROC 0.9009 vs 0.9022, because table.csv features differ at float32 level (max 2e-5) and land on HGB bin edges. The same refit of tab_mem moves its held-out AUROC by +0.002 [-0.003, +0.007], so bag+graph carries refit noise of that size.

The time-matching definition decides RQ2. With the plan's rounds-to-cut bins the clock alone reaches 0.716 (0.635 on night_train CV). At equal rounds-to-cut, late-deadline configs sit at later absolute rounds, and in the two earliest bins (66% of the pairs) almost all positives come from cut 23/26 configs. With the harness round bins the clock is 0.530, and all five monitors beat it (+0.19 to +0.26, p <= 0.0002, 4/4 splits). Under the pre-registered plan definition, nothing survives Holm.
LLM monitors read raw message text, including task words. The headline GNN and tabular models exclude the task lexicon, so the information sets differ.

zs:global_full sees an implicit clock (the full transcript). Its Spearman correlation with the round is 0.83 on held-out rows, the highest of any predictor (clock 0.73), so its pooled AUROC partly reflects time.
Haiku is also one of the two jury judges (DeepSeek + Haiku) behind the GNN and tabular features. The GNN-vs-LLM comparison is therefore not between independent information sources.

In ood_seed the trigger (injection via tool output) is not in the communication. Within round bins the trained monitors are near chance there (harness tAUROC 0.535-0.564); the zero-shot monitors reach 0.64-0.70.

Few configs per split: 12/8/8/8, and only 7/4/7/5 hold a positive. Per-split signs and the >=3/4 rule are fragile: a1 reaches 3/4 only through branch +0.0005. The within-mixed statistic rests on 9 configs and 45 positives (CI widths 0.24-0.56). A percentile cluster bootstrap with 36 clusters may be somewhat too narrow; that cannot change the null verdicts, but it means the uncorrected secondary p-values should not be read strictly.

Robustness of the null result: split-stratified bootstrap gives smallest Holm p 0.059, and bootstrap seeds 1-3 give smallest Holm p 0.081-0.092. Row-level DeLong would call 7 of the 11 primary tests significant; the cluster/DeLong SE ratio is 1.3-2.1, so DeLong is anti-conservative here.

Thresholds come from different pools. Trained models use night_train ID-OOF CV predictions, and for gnn5/hybrid that is the GNN team's 4-run CV proxy, not the 5-seed final model. Zero-shot monitors use night_train+night_val raw scores. Realised held-out row FPRs range 0.029-0.094, so the recalls are not at equal FPR. Raw zero-shot scores are uncalibrated (Brier not comparable).
The zero-shot prompt was frozen on 8 night_train dev runs: untrained, but not blind to the training split.

Deviations from plan §5, made by instruction: rows are the GNN harness rows (branch prefixes once) instead of llm_monitor.evaluate's (prefixes three times), and the GNN models were trained on night_train only, not refit on train+val. Plan criterion 1 (the CV CI) is not evaluated here; the Holm-corrected held-out bootstrap replaces it.
The mean-of-ranks combination is exploratory and post hoc. It is transductive in the ranks (uses the held-out score distribution, no labels).
